title: Britain’s royal family wracked by fresh turmoil after brief summer respite | CNN
text:
Source: CNN

King Charles wanted all eyes on AI, as he prepared to host amajor summitto discuss the controversial technology.

But those hopes were shattered after a fresh royal scandal hit the front pages hours before Thursday’s meeting started, threatening to overshadow the tech gathering and throwing the clan into turmoil.

“Charles’s astonishing outburst days after Diana’s death,” the Daily Mail’s front page read, while the Daily Telegraph wrote, “Palace hits back at Diana’s brother.”

Buckingham Palace issued arare rebuttalon Wednesday after Charles Spencer, the brother of the late Princess Diana, said the then Prince of Wales had told him days after her death that “we’ll forget her soon enough,” according to an extract published by the Daily Mail from his forthcoming book.

Spencer claims Charles launched into a “stream of anger” over the phone following Diana’s death, after Spencer argued his sister would not have wanted William and Harry to take part in her funeral procession.

Fresh claims published Thursday in another extract by the Daily Mail alleged Charles “sounded giddily elated – like a lottery winner” when speaking to Spencer on the night of Diana’s death. CNN has not seen Spencer’s upcoming book “Swan Song: Diana, My Sister” ahead of its publication next week.

The late Princess of Wales died in August 1997 after suffering internal injuries resulting from a high-speed car crash in Paris. Her sons, ages 15 and 12 at the time, walked in the funeral procession days later alongside Charles, from whom she was divorced.

Spencer’s memoir casts back to a particularly sensitive period for the royals.

Known as the “People’s Princess,” Diana was a beloved figure in the United Kingdom and around the world whose untimely death, age 36, stunned the nation. The royal family’s initial response to her death was criticized as overly insular, sparking a constitutional crisis and widespread public backlash.

In response to the memoir, Buckingham Palace called into question Spencer’s personal judgement following Diana’s death – an unusual intervention, even in the palace’s own words, and one which speaks to the scale of the crisis in the eyes of “the firm,” as the royal family is sometimes described.

“While we do not comment on books as a matter of principle, His Majesty is mindful that the pain of fraternal grief can cloud reason, affect judgment and color memory in ways others do not recognize, even many years after such a loss,” a palace spokesperson said.

For some royal observers, the firm’s response echoed the late Queen Elizabeth II’srebukeof several damning claims made by the Duke and Duchess of Sussex in 2021, after the couple left the UK for North America following their step back from royal life.

“Recollections may vary,” the Queen said at the time.

Extracts from the book also detail Spencer’s perception of his sister’s unhappy relationship with Charles, including allegations that she found a bracelet her then-fiancé had bought for Camilla, and later tried to break off the engagement. It also alleges Charles called her “chubby” just after their engagement, a comment Diana, who suffered from an eating disorder, found “devastating.” Many of these anecdotes have previously been reported by various biographers and outlets. The palace told CNN Thursday it had nothing further to add to its previous statement.

This year got off to a particularly bumpy start for the British royals, including thearrestof King Charles’ brother, Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor, on his 66th birthday on suspicion of misconduct in public office while the former prince was a trade envoy for Britain.

Mountbatten-Windsor stepped down from the role in 2011 after coming under severe criticism over his ties to convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein. He has vehemently denied any and all wrongdoing in his dealings with Epstein, and has denied any personal gain from his role as a British trade envoy, according to British media reports.

After a quieter summer, the clan would have been hoping for a scandal-free end to the year, but the upcoming release of Spencer’s memoir, shortly after the surprise return of Prince Harry and Meghan to the country presents a number of fresh headaches for the family.

Amid the turmoil, senior royals carried out a busy day of engagements Thursday.

The same day, Harry made his first public outing since returning to the UK with his family last month, attending the inaugural Invictus Spirit Awards, a gala honoring wounded, injured, and sick servicemembers, veterans, and community supporters in London. Celebrities including comedian James Corden, singer Jess Glynne and Ross Kemp were in attendance.

Neither Harry nor Meghan are acting as working royals following their return, but the prince’s appearance indicates he isn’t planning to shy away from the public eye.

Charlesissued a letterearlier this month clarifying that the couple should be treated as “private citizens,” a move which was said to “surprise” Harry and Meghan, according to a spokesperson for the Sussexes.

The couple and their children, Prince Archie, 7, and Princess Lilibet, 5, have largely kept out of the spotlight since their return.

But they have not proved immune from all issues, notablyswitching their children’s schooljust days into the start of the new academic year, citing security practicalities.

That decision came after British media reported Meghan had been granted a new security review for the first time since quitting royal duties – another sticking point between the couple and the broader clan.

Meanwhile, the Prince and Princess of Wales, Prince William and his wife Kate, made their first official visit to the Isle of Bute in Scotland on Thursday.

This story has been updated to clarify the date of the book release.

CNN’s Lauren Kent and Issy Ronald contributed reporting.

CNN’s Lauren Kent and Issy Ronald contributed reporting.
